scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.description: Normal boot: verified kernel and initramfs, boot info check, own GDT/IDT/stacks, allocator, page tables, reclaim, self-tests, timer, TEST PASS.

patterns: ^NANOX: kernel sha256 {kernel_sha256}$
^NANOX: bootinfo acpi_rsdp=0x[0-9a-f]+$
^NANOX: initramfs ok entries=10 bytes=[0-9]+ sha256={initrd_sha256}$
^NANOX: initramfs release "NANOX-OS initramfs M3"$
^NANOX: cpu gdt\+tss\+idt loaded
^NANOX: selftest breakpoint ok resumed=2$
^NANOX: pmm ok span_pages=[0-9]+ managed=[1-9][0-9]*
^NANOX: vmm ok root=0x[0-9a-f]+ physmap=0xffff800000000000 .* text=r-x rodata=r-- data=rw- guards=4 null=unmapped$
^NANOX: pmm reclaimed boot_reclaimable=([1-9][0-9]*) loader_stack=16 pages poisoned=[1-9][0-9]* free=[0-9]+$
^NANOX: selftest pmm ok pages=256
^NANOX: selftest vmm ok
^NANOX: timer ok source=lapic vector=0x40 hz=100 lapic_per_10ms=[0-9]+ window_ms=300 ticks=[0-9]+ expected=30

scenarios.name: fail
scenarios.description: Kernel reports a deliberate test failure (nanox.test=fail).

scenarios.name: unknown-test
scenarios.description: Unknown nanox.test value is a test failure, not a silent pass.

scenarios.name: panic
scenarios.description: Kernel panic path (nanox.test=panic).

patterns: ^NANOX: PANIC requested by nanox.test=panic$

scenarios.name: hang
scenarios.description: Kernel halts forever; only the harness timeout ends the run.

patterns: ^NANOX: kernel_main
^NANOX: test hang

scenarios.name: missing-kernel
scenarios.description: KERNEL.ELF absent from the ESP.

scenarios.name: corrupt-kernel
scenarios.description: One byte of KERNEL.ELF flipped after the manifest was written.

scenarios.name: framebuffer
scenarios.description: Canonical config plus one VGA device: exercises the optional framebuffer fields.

patterns: ^NANOX: bootinfo framebuffer [0-9]+x[0-9]+ pitch=[0-9]+ format=[12] base=0x[0-9a-f]+$

scenarios.name: missing-initrd
scenarios.description: INITRD.IMG absent from the ESP.

scenarios.name: corrupt-initrd
scenarios.description: One byte of INITRD.IMG flipped after the manifest was written.

scenarios.name: bad-initrd
scenarios.description: Initramfs that matches the manifest but is not a cpio archive (150 bytes of text): rejected by the kernel.

image.initrd_text: NANOX test: this text is not a cpio newc archive. NANOX test: this text is not a cpio newc archive. NANOX test: this text is not a cpio newc archive.

patterns: ^NANOX: PANIC initramfs invalid: E_MAGIC at offset 0$

scenarios.name: ud
scenarios.description: Deliberate #UD (ud2) must be caught by the kernel IDT and reported.

scenarios.name: gp
scenarios.description: Deliberate #GP (load through a non-canonical address).

scenarios.name: divzero
scenarios.description: Deliberate #DE (division by zero).

scenarios.name: pagefault
scenarios.description: Deliberate write to an address the kernel never maps: #PF with verifiable diagnostics.

patterns: ^NANOX: EXCEPTION #PF present=0 write=1 user=0 reserved=0 fetch=0$
^NANOX: EXCEPTION #PF mapping va=0x00000000dead0000 not-mapped$

scenarios.name: nullderef
scenarios.description: Read through a null pointer: the null page is not mapped.

patterns: ^NANOX: EXCEPTION #PF mapping va=0x0000000000000000 not-mapped$

scenarios.name: wprotect
scenarios.description: Write to .rodata: mapped read-only, CR0.WP set.

patterns: ^NANOX: EXCEPTION #PF present=1 write=1 user=0 reserved=0 fetch=0$
^NANOX: EXCEPTION #PF mapping va=0x[0-9a-f]+ pa=0x[0-9a-f]+ size=4K perms=r--$

scenarios.name: nxexec
scenarios.description: Jump into writable data: mapped non-executable (EFER.NXE).

patterns: ^NANOX: EXCEPTION #PF present=1 write=0 user=0 reserved=0 fetch=1$
^NANOX: EXCEPTION #PF mapping va=0x[0-9a-f]+ pa=0x[0-9a-f]+ size=4K perms=rw-$

scenarios.name: stackoverflow
scenarios.description: Unbounded recursion hits the unmapped guard page below the boot stack; #DF on its IST stack.

patterns: ^NANOX: EXCEPTION stack overflow: guard page of stack boot hit at 0x[0-9a-f]+$

scenarios.name: doublefree
scenarios.description: Freeing a page twice: the physical allocator refuses and the kernel panics.

patterns: ^NANOX: PANIC pmm: free of page 0x[0-9a-f]+ rejected: E_DOUBLE_FREE$

scenarios.name: timer-masked
scenarios.description: Timer LVT deliberately left masked: the kernel's timer check must detect missing interrupts.

patterns: ^NANOX: TEST FAIL timer: no timer interrupts in the window \(ticks=0 expected=30\)$

scenarios.name: m2-user
scenarios.description: M2 criterion 1: bin/hello from the initramfs runs in ring 3 in its own address space, prints through debug_write and exits 0; the kernel reaps it and the allocator and page-table counters return to their values before the task.

patterns: ^NANOX: sched ok tasks=kmain#1,idle#2 preempt=on slice_ticks=2 hz=100 user_fpu=off gdt_user=0x1b/0x23 syscall_vector=0x80$
^NANOX: m2-user spawn hello#3 path=bin/hello size=[0-9]+ entry=0x0000008000000000$
^NANOX: m2-user address space hello#3 root=0x[0-9a-f]+ kernel_root=0x[0-9a-f]+ code=user,r-x stack=user,rw- kernel_root_maps_them=no pages_in_use=[1-9][0-9]*$
^NANOX: USER hello#3: hello from ring 3: cpl=3 task=3$
^NANOX: USER hello#3: code=0x8000000[0-9a-f]{{3}} data=0x8000002000 stack=0x7ffffffe[0-9a-f]{{4}} data_ok=yes bss_ok=yes$
^NANOX: USER hello#3: exiting with code 0$
^NANOX: task hello#3 exited code=0 ticks=[0-9]+ preempted=0 syscalls=6$
^NANOX: m2-user resources before free_pages=([0-9]+) tables=([0-9]+) tasks=2 vmos=0 endpoints=0$[\s\S]*^NANOX: m2-user resources after free_pages=\1 tables=\2 tasks=2 vmos=0 endpoints=0$
^NANOX: m2-user ok task=hello#3 exit=0 syscalls=6 pages_in_use=[1-9][0-9]* free_pages_restored=[0-9]+$

scenarios.name: m2-sched
scenarios.description: M2 criterion 2: three bin/spin tasks that never yield or block are interleaved by the timer (preemptive round robin), each finishes with the result the kernel computed independently.

patterns: ^NANOX: sched ok tasks=kmain#1,idle#2 preempt=on slice_ticks=2 hz=100 user_fpu=off gdt_user=0x1b/0x23 syscall_vector=0x80$
^NANOX: m2-sched expect spin-a#3 iterations=200000000 result=(0x[0-9a-f]{{16}})$[\s\S]*^NANOX: USER spin-a#3: done index=0 iterations=200000000 result=\1 ok$
^NANOX: m2-sched expect spin-b#4 iterations=200000000 result=(0x[0-9a-f]{{16}})$[\s\S]*^NANOX: USER spin-b#4: done index=1 iterations=200000000 result=\1 ok$
^NANOX: m2-sched expect spin-c#5 iterations=200000000 result=(0x[0-9a-f]{{16}})$[\s\S]*^NANOX: USER spin-c#5: done index=2 iterations=200000000 result=\1 ok$
^NANOX: task spin-a#3 exited code=0 ticks=[0-9]+ preempted=[1-9][0-9]* syscalls=6$
^NANOX: task spin-b#4 exited code=0 ticks=[0-9]+ preempted=[1-9][0-9]* syscalls=6$
^NANOX: task spin-c#5 exited code=0 ticks=[0-9]+ preempted=[1-9][0-9]* syscalls=6$
^NANOX: m2-sched progress order latest_first=[0-9]+ earliest_last=[0-9]+ preempted=[1-9][0-9]*,[1-9][0-9]*,[1-9][0-9]*$
^NANOX: m2-sched resources before free_pages=([0-9]+) tables=([0-9]+) tasks=2 vmos=0 endpoints=0$[\s\S]*^NANOX: m2-sched resources after free_pages=\1 tables=\2 tasks=2 vmos=0 endpoints=0$
^NANOX: m2-sched ok tasks=3 exited=3 yields=0 interleaved=yes switches=[0-9]+ preemptions=[1-9][0-9]*$

scenarios.name: m2-sched-nopreempt
scenarios.description: Negative control for m2-sched: the same tasks with preemption disabled run one after another, and the interleaving check must fail.

patterns: ^NANOX: sched ok tasks=kmain#1,idle#2 preempt=off slice_ticks=2 hz=100 user_fpu=off gdt_user=0x1b/0x23 syscall_vector=0x80$
^NANOX: USER spin-c#5: done index=2 iterations=200000000 result=0x[0-9a-f]{{16}} ok$
^NANOX: m2-sched-nopreempt progress order latest_first=[0-9]+ earliest_last=[0-9]+ preempted=0,0,0$
^NANOX: TEST FAIL m2-sched-nopreempt: tasks did not interleave: a task finished before another reported progress

scenarios.name: m2-ipc
scenarios.description: M2 criterion 3: bin/ipc-send sends a message and a memory-object handle reduced to READ|MAP to bin/ipc-recv, which receives both intact with exactly those rights, maps the page read-only and is refused write mapping and duplication.

patterns: ^NANOX: sched ok tasks=kmain#1,idle#2 preempt=on slice_ticks=2 hz=100 user_fpu=off gdt_user=0x1b/0x23 syscall_vector=0x80$
^NANOX: m2-ipc endpoint ipc-send#4 handle=0x[0-9a-f]+ rights=0x20, ipc-recv#3 handle=0x[0-9a-f]+ rights=0x40$
^NANOX: m2-ipc ipc-recv#3 blocked in receive on the endpoint, starting ipc-send#4$
^NANOX: USER ipc-send#4: send granting an extra right \(0x25\): EACCESS \(expected EACCESS\)$
^NANOX: ipc send by ipc-send#4 len=48 handle=vmo sender_rights=0x1f requested=0x5 queued=0x5$
^NANOX: USER ipc-send#4: send len=48 granting 0x5: ok$
^NANOX: USER ipc-send#4: close of the sent handle: EBADHANDLE \(expected EBADHANDLE\)$
^NANOX: ipc recv by ipc-recv#3 len=48 from=#4 handle=0x[0-9a-f]+ rights=0x5$
^NANOX: USER ipc-recv#3: received len=48 from=#4 \(expected #4\) message intact: "NANOX M2: one page of memory for you \(read-only\)"$
^NANOX: USER ipc-recv#3: handle=0x[0-9a-f]+ rights=0x5 expected=0x5$
^NANOX: USER ipc-recv#3: map read-only at 0x20000000000: ok, page contents match the sender's$
^NANOX: USER ipc-recv#3: map read-write: EACCESS \(expected EACCESS\), duplicate: EACCESS \(expected EACCESS\)$
^NANOX: USER ipc-recv#3: verdict ok$
^NANOX: task ipc-send#4 exited code=0
^NANOX: task ipc-recv#3 exited code=0
^NANOX: m2-ipc resources before free_pages=([0-9]+) tables=([0-9]+) tasks=2 vmos=0 endpoints=0$[\s\S]*^NANOX: m2-ipc resources after free_pages=\1 tables=\2 tasks=2 vmos=0 endpoints=0$
^NANOX: m2-ipc ok message and handle delivered, rights reduced to 0x5$

scenarios.name: m2-ipc-overgrant
scenarios.description: Negative control for m2-ipc: the kernel deliberately delivers the handle with all of the sender's rights; the receiver must detect it and the run must fail.

patterns: ^NANOX: m2-ipc-overgrant fault injection: transferred handles keep all sender rights$
^NANOX: ipc send by ipc-send#4 len=48 handle=vmo sender_rights=0x1f requested=0x5 queued=0x1f$
^NANOX: USER ipc-recv#3: handle=0x[0-9a-f]+ rights=0x1f expected=0x5$
^NANOX: USER ipc-recv#3: verdict FAILED$
^NANOX: TEST FAIL m2-ipc-overgrant: task ipc-recv#3 did not exit normally with code 0 \(end=1 code=2\)$

scenarios.name: m3-agent
scenarios.description: M3 criteria 2, 3, 4, 6: the host bridge's model adapter (mock) turns the request 'list tasks, start the test workload, measure it, stop it' into NCI calls; bin/core executes them in the guest and verifies every end state; the host checks the result independently and the trace is complete.

patterns: ^NANOX: m3 boot_id=[0-9a-f]{{16}} bridge=com2 port=0x2f8 events=on kill=on dedup=on$
^NANOX: USER core#4: ready task/[0-9a-f]{{16}}/4 dedup=on: waiting for NCI requests on the bridge$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act t1-1 task.list SUCCEEDED$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act t1-2 task.spawn PLANNED call=SOV_TASK_SPAWN path=bin/load$
^NANOX: USER load#5: load started: computing until terminated$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act t1-2 task.spawn SUCCEEDED task=5 state=(ready|running) ran=yes events=created,started$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act t1-3 task.measure SUCCEEDED cpu_ticks=[1-9][0-9]* window_ticks=[0-9]+$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act t1-4 task.terminate PLANNED call=TASK_KILL h=0x[0-9a-f]+ rev=2$
^NANOX: task load#5 killed: by task #4 through a task handle$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act t1-4 task.terminate SUCCEEDED state=reaped end=killed events=killed,reaped handle=released$
^NANOX: USER core#4: session closed host_checks=ok reason=- actions=[0-9]+ replayed=0 verify_failures=0 exit=0$
^NANOX: m3-serve resources before free_pages=([0-9]+) tables=([0-9]+) tasks=3 vmos=0 endpoints=0$[\s\S]*^NANOX: m3-serve resources after free_pages=\1 tables=\2 tasks=3 vmos=0 endpoints=0$
^NANOX: m3-serve ok core#4 exit=0 resources_restored=yes$

scenarios.name: m3-nci
scenarios.description: M3 criterion 1: every operation of the first NCI set over the bridge, the kernel's state events of a spawned and terminated task (created, started, killed, reaped, gapless), the task engine's action states and action.status, rejected malformed requests, memory returned.

patterns: ^NANOX: m3 boot_id=[0-9a-f]{{16}} bridge=com2 port=0x2f8 events=on kill=on dedup=on$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act r-1 system.describe SUCCEEDED$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act nci-term task.terminate SUCCEEDED state=reaped end=killed events=killed,reaped handle=released$
^NANOX: USER core#4: status r-[0-9]+ request=nci-term known=yes state=SUCCEEDED$
^NANOX: USER core#4: reject id=r-[0-9]+: unknown operation frobnicate.now$
^NANOX: USER core#4: reject id=bad-1: duplicate_argument$
^NANOX: USER core#4: session closed host_checks=ok reason=- actions=[0-9]+ replayed=0 verify_failures=0 exit=0$
^NANOX: m3-serve resources before free_pages=([0-9]+) tables=([0-9]+) tasks=3 vmos=0 endpoints=0$[\s\S]*^NANOX: m3-serve resources after free_pages=\1 tables=\2 tasks=3 vmos=0 endpoints=0$
^NANOX: m3-serve ok core#4 exit=0 resources_restored=yes$

scenarios.name: m3-events-off
scenarios.description: Negative control for m3-nci: the kernel records no state events; the executor's event checks and the host's event checks must fail.

patterns: ^NANOX: m3 boot_id=[0-9a-f]{{16}} bridge=com2 port=0x2f8 events=off kill=on dedup=on$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act r-[0-9]+ task.spawn FAILED code=VERIFY_FAILED detail=no_created_event effects=applied$
^NANOX: USER core#4: session closed host_checks=fail reason=spawn .*verify_failures=[1-9] exit=3$
^NANOX: TEST FAIL m3-events-off: core#4 exited with code 3: the executor's end-state verification failed$

scenarios.name: m3-faults
scenarios.description: M3 criterion 5: stale references (other boot, never issued id, ended task, stale revision) are refused without effect; a repeated request id is answered from the executor's record without executing again; a lost response is resolved through action.status and a replay; a lost (never delivered) request is unknown to the executor and executes once when sent.

patterns: ^NANOX: m3 boot_id=[0-9a-f]{{16}} bridge=com2 port=0x2f8 events=on kill=on dedup=on$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act r-[0-9]+ task.inspect FAILED code=STALE_REF effects=none$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act r-[0-9]+ task.inspect FAILED code=NOT_FOUND effects=none$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act r-[0-9]+ task.terminate FAILED code=CONFLICT detail=rev_2 effects=none$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act f-spawn-b task.spawn REPLAYED stored_state=SUCCEEDED \(not executed again\)$
^NANOX: USER core#4: reject id=f-spawn-b: ID_REUSED$
^NANOX: USER core#4: status f-kill-a-st request=f-kill-a known=yes state=SUCCEEDED$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act f-kill-a task.terminate REPLAYED stored_state=SUCCEEDED \(not executed again\)$
^NANOX: USER core#4: status r-[0-9]+ request=f-kill-b known=no state=-$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act r-[0-9]+ task.terminate FAILED code=GONE effects=none$
^NANOX: USER core#4: session closed host_checks=ok reason=- actions=[0-9]+ replayed=2 verify_failures=0 exit=0$
^NANOX: m3-serve resources before free_pages=([0-9]+) tables=([0-9]+) tasks=3 vmos=0 endpoints=0$[\s\S]*^NANOX: m3-serve resources after free_pages=\1 tables=\2 tasks=3 vmos=0 endpoints=0$
^NANOX: m3-serve ok core#4 exit=0 resources_restored=yes$

scenarios.name: m3-nodedup
scenarios.description: Negative control for m3-faults: the executor does not deduplicate requests; the repeated spawn starts a second task and the host's retry check must fail.

problems: ^retry_created_second_task: after spawning A and B \(B requested twice\) 3 load tasks are alive$

patterns: ^NANOX: m3 boot_id=[0-9a-f]{{16}} bridge=com2 port=0x2f8 events=on kill=on dedup=off$
^NANOX: USER core#4: session closed host_checks=fail reason=retry_not_replayed .*verify_failures=0 exit=4$
^NANOX: TEST FAIL m3-nodedup: core#4 exited with code 4: the host bridge reported failed host-side checks$

scenarios.name: m3-model-down
scenarios.description: M3 criterion 5: the model provider is unavailable; the host task fails as model_unavailable after the configured attempts, no action reaches the guest, and the guest stays controllable without the model.

patterns: ^NANOX: m3 boot_id=[0-9a-f]{{16}} bridge=com2 port=0x2f8 events=on kill=on dedup=on$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act r-1 system.describe SUCCEEDED$
^NANOX: USER core#4: session closed host_checks=ok reason=- actions=2 replayed=0 verify_failures=0 exit=0$
^NANOX: m3-serve ok core#4 exit=0 resources_restored=yes$

scenarios.name: m3-kill-noop
scenarios.description: Negative control for m3-agent (criterion 4): the kernel's kill call reports success without an effect; the executor's end-state check must refuse to report success and the run must fail.

patterns: ^NANOX: m3 boot_id=[0-9a-f]{{16}} bridge=com2 port=0x2f8 events=on kill=noop dedup=on$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act t1-4 task.terminate VERIFYING result=ok$
^NANOX: USER core#4: act t1-4 task.terminate FAILED code=VERIFY_FAILED detail=still_running effects=unknown$
^NANOX: m3-kill-noop leftover task load#5 state=[0-9]: terminating$
^NANOX: TEST FAIL m3-kill-noop: core#4 exited with code 3: the executor's end-state verification failed$

scenarios.name: m4-blk
scenarios.description: M4 virtio-blk driver: boot disk (read-only, GPT) and data disk (serial nanox-data) found over PCI; the read-only disk refuses a write; 8 blocks written, flushed, read back and restored; the emulated volatile cache of the crash-test layer holds a write until the flush.

patterns: ^NANOX: blk 00:[0-9a-f]{{2}}\.0 virtio-blk id=0x10(01|42) serial="" sectors=131072 features=0x[0-9a-f]+ ro=yes flush=yes queue=16$
^NANOX: blk 00:[0-9a-f]{{2}}\.0 virtio-blk id=0x10(01|42) serial="nanox-data" sectors=2048 features=0x[0-9a-f]+ ro=no flush=yes queue=16$
^NANOX: m4-blk boot disk sectors=131072 mbr=55aa gpt="EFI PART" write=(ioerr|unsupp)$
^NANOX: m4-blk data disk serial="nanox-data" blocks=256 write\+flush\+readback=ok blocks=248-255 range_check=ok$
^NANOX: m4-blk test cache pending=1 device_before_flush=old device_after_flush=new ops=2$
^NANOX: m4-blk restored requests=[0-9]+ errors=0$

scenarios.name: m4-crash
scenarios.description: M4 crash consistency: the built-in workload of bin/core (configuration, blobs, pins, task.spawn/terminate with write-ahead records, reuse of released blocks) is stopped before every one of its write/flush operations, with every persistence policy of the unflushed writes that changes the outcome there (all lost, all kept, newest torn, only newest kept); after each stop a check boot must recover a generation between the last one reported saved and the last one begun, with exactly the content of the model of that generation, confirmed by the host-side reader and both consistency checks.

scenarios.name: m4-persist
scenarios.description: M4 criterion 2: boot 1 sets configuration, runs task.spawn/terminate (write-ahead and final records), stores a blob and pins a generation; boot 2 on the same data disk finds the configuration, the history of boot 1 (commit log with its boot id, pinned generation readable), the task records (action.status known, persisted, restored), answers a repeated boot-1 request from its record without running it again, rejects a boot-1 id with another request, and commits the next generation.

scenarios.name: m4-persist-amnesia
scenarios.description: Negative control of criterion 2: boot 2 gets a freshly formatted data disk instead of the one boot 1 wrote; the host checks of persistence (configuration, task records, replay of the boot-1 request) must fail.

patterns: ^NANOX: TEST FAIL m4-serve: core#4 exited with code 4:

scenarios.name: m4-corrupt-root
scenarios.description: M4 criterion 3 (damaged root): after boot 1 committed generations 2 and 3, the harness flips a byte of the root block of generation 3; boot 2 must reject it (bad_root), fall back to generation 2 in the other slot, report the fallback, and commit generation 4 into the damaged slot.

scenarios.name: m4-unmountable
scenarios.description: M4 criterion 3 (no valid root): both superblocks damaged after boot 1; boot 2 must refuse the store (no_valid_root, both slots bad_crc), fail store operations with NO_STORE and no effects, keep serving the other operations, and leave the disk untouched.

scenarios.name: m4-full
scenarios.description: M4 criterion 3 (full store): 32 KiB blobs until NO_SPACE; the failed put has no effect and no record, the last blob and the consistency check are intact; deletes and prunes (allowed to use the reserve) release space, a new put succeeds; boot 2 finds the same generation and valid blobs.

scenarios.name: m4-retention
scenarios.description: M4 criterion 4: the retention window (4 generations) and pins: a pinned generation outside the window stays readable, an unpinned one is PRUNED, unpin and store.prune release blocks, the commit log keeps the entries of released generations marked pruned.

scenarios.name: m4-crash-noflush
scenarios.description: Negative control of the crash sweep: the block layer reports every flush as done without writing the emulated volatile cache out; a stop right after each generation reported saved, losing the unflushed writes, must lose saved generations.
